purpose: Calibrate workload fidelity before capacity experiments. Not a production-fix verdict.

ingress_coverage.scope: One-minute slices every 15 minutes, not continuous ingress history or exact request-arrival replay.

confirmed: Production client demand, background refresh records and origin DB query counts are distinct populations.
Page API/limit mix and key diversity materially differ from the old stress test.
Cache locality changes across the cycle; a fixed hot-key percentage is inadequate.
remaining: One-minute log samples do not establish all arrivals between samples or client crawl/connection lifetimes.
Measured page frequency model maps ranks to different staging cursor positions; body-size distribution and origin query rate must be calibrated.
Protocol mix is measured; TCP connection reuse, compression negotiation and client retry behavior remain unmeasured.
Search term selectivity, incremental-sync age/cursor mix, detail calls and concurrent publishes still need matching; old default search/update policies are not qualified.
Baseline must use the production release and CPU reservations/placement; the last candidate run was not this control.
Natural scale-up/down and sustained-duration acceptance remain untested under a calibrated workload.

next_gate: First qualify a production-aligned baseline against measured API/limit mix, key diversity/cache outcomes, wire/decoded body sizes, origin query rates, CPU pressure and acquisition delays. Run the candidate only after baseline fidelity is established. Keep the old 4500-rps workload labeled as stress, not production acceptance.
